title: Rakesh Sharma v. State of U.P.
coram: Krishna Murari, J.; Ashwani Kumar Mishra, J.
disposition: Demand notice quashed; fresh provisional assessment with hearing directed
headnote: After a theft raid and compounding, the licensee treated an unserved provisional assessment as final and issued a Section 3 recovery demand. The Division Bench held that want of service deprived the consumer of the right to object. Following Ashok Kumar on Electricity Supply Code, 2005 theft-assessment procedure, it quashed the demand and directed a fresh served provisional assessment, time to object, a hearing, and a reasoned final order.
facts: A surprise raid at the petitioner's premises found theft of electricity by connecting a cable bypassing the meter. He paid Rs.10,000 as compounding charges. The licensee made a provisional assessment dated 26 May 2014 and sent it by speed post; it returned unserved with an endorsement that the residence was locked. No objection was filed. The assessment was treated as final, and a demand notice dated 21 July 2014 under Section 3 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958, seeking Rs.36,630, was issued. He challenged that notice.

reusable_constructions.construction: An unserved provisional assessment in a theft case cannot be treated as final; the consumer must be served and given time to object and a hearing before a reasoned final assessment under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

A recovery demand under Section 3 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertakings (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958, founded on such an unserved assessment is liable to be quashed, with the assessment redone after service, objection and hearing.

holding_units.topic: theft assessment — service of provisional assessment
holding_units.holding: Where the provisional assessment for theft of electricity is not served, treating it as final and issuing a Section 3 Dues Recovery demand is unsustainable. The licensee must issue a fresh provisional assessment, serve it, allow fifteen days to object, fix a date for hearing, and then pass a reasoned final assessment after considering any objection, in light of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as explained in Ashok Kumar.

not_decided.point: Merits and quantum of the theft assessment
not_decided.note: Remitted for fresh provisional assessment, service, objection, hearing and reasoned final order.
